# single_include/

`single_include/gauge15/sfv.hpp` is a **generated file** — one self-contained
header containing the entire library, for the common header-only-library
convenience of "copy one file into your project and `#include` it,"
following the same convention as `nlohmann/json`'s `single_include/`.

**Do not edit this file directly.** `include/gauge15/*.hpp` is the real
source; this is a build artifact of it, produced by
`tools/amalgamate.py`:

```sh
python3 tools/amalgamate.py > single_include/gauge15/sfv.hpp
```

## Why generated, not hand-maintained

Hand-maintaining two copies of the same library — one split into files
for development, one concatenated for distribution — guarantees they
eventually drift: a fix applied to one and forgotten in the other. The
amalgamation script concatenates the real headers in dependency order,
strips each file's own include guard (replacing all of them with a
single guard for the whole output) and internal `#include "gauge15/...")`
lines, and deduplicates external `#include <...>` lines into one block —
deterministically, from the real source, every time.

## Verification, not assumption

Before trusting a generated file, it should actually be tested, not just
inspected for looking right. The full test suite (all 1,395 conformance
checks), both GCC and Clang, the same stricter warning set used
elsewhere in this project, ASan+UBSan, and a fuzzing pass all ran
successfully against `single_include/gauge15/sfv.hpp` specifically (not just
`include/gauge15/`) before this file was committed:

```sh
g++ -std=c++20 -Isingle_include -Itests tests/test-key-generated.cpp -o t && ./t
# 972/972 checks passed (key-generated.json conformance, all 640 cases)
```

If you regenerate this file (e.g. after changing `include/gauge15/`), re-run
at least one test binary against `-Isingle_include` before trusting the
new output the same way.

## Using it

Copy `single_include/gauge15/sfv.hpp` into your project and:

```cpp
#include "gauge15/sfv.hpp"
// same API as the multi-file version -- sfv::parse_item, sfv::parse_list,
// sfv::parse_dictionary, sfv::serialize(...)
```

No other files needed.
